title: AgentTuning: Enabling Generalized Agent Abilities for LLMs
data_curation: AgentInstruct is built from 6 agent tasks (ALFWorld, WebShop, Mind2Web, Knowledge Graph, Operating System, Database), yielding 1,866 filtered interaction trajectories from 35,341 instructions. For tasks with train splits (ALFWorld/WebShop/Mind2Web/KG) the split is used directly; for OS and DB the authors use Task Derivation (deriving from the BIRD text-to-SQL benchmark) and Self-Instruct (GPT-4 proposes OS tasks plus reference solutions and eval scripts). Trajectories are collected by running GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613) as the agent under ReAct prompting with 1-shot examples; Mind2Web partly uses gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 for budget. Filtering keeps trajectories with reward r=1 (r>=2/3 for the harder Mind2Web); a 7B ablation shows filtered data (held-in 1.96, held-out 0.65) beats unfiltered (1.34, 0.47). General-domain data comes from ShareGPT (57,096 GPT-3.5 + 3,670 GPT-4 conversations, sampled 4:1 GPT-3.5:GPT-4). A 10-gram contamination check (Llama-2-style) finds no leakage.
curriculum: A single-stage hybrid supervised fine-tuning recipe rather than a multi-stage RL/preference pipeline. AgentInstruct (agent trajectories) is mixed with ShareGPT (general-domain) instructions at ratio eta, where eta is the agent-data fraction; eta was scanned 0-1 in 0.1 steps on the 7B model and eta=0.2 chosen for best held-out performance. All data is standardized to a multi-turn chatbot format (following Vicuna) and loss is computed only on model outputs. Base models are Llama-2-{7,13,70}b-chat (chosen for instruction-following), trained with Megatron-LM, AdamW, cosine schedule with 2% warmup, batch 64 at 4096 seq len, LR 5e-5 (7B/13B) and 1e-5 (70B); 70B adds pipeline parallelism atop tensor parallelism. The rationale: general capabilities are pivotal for agent generalization, and training solely on agent data collapses both general and held-out performance.
method: AgentTuning is a hybrid instruction-tuning method that activates latent agent abilities in already-aligned LLMs without harming general skills. The objective is a weighted log-likelihood: J(theta) = eta * E_(x,y)~D_agent[log pi_theta(y|x)] + (1-eta) * E_(x,y)~D_general[log pi_theta(y|x)]. The agent data consists of ReAct-style trajectories where each step pairs a thought with an action, so the model learns the reasoning leading to tool/environment actions rather than just final answers. The central finding is that Llama-2-chat already has agent capability but misfires on elementary errors (invalid actions, repetition, refusals); AgentTuning largely removes these, suggesting activation rather than overfitting. It is framed as the first end-to-end attempt to instruction-tune LLMs on interaction trajectories spanning multiple agent tasks, producing the open AgentLM-7B/13B/70B.
eval_metrics: Evaluation uses 6 held-in tasks from AgentBench (ALFWorld, WebShop, Mind2Web, KG, OS, Database) and 6 held-out tasks (SciWorld, MiniWoB++, WebArena, HotpotQA, ReWOO, Digital Card Game) with task-specific metrics (Success Rate, Reward, Step SR, F1); overall scores are normalized weighted averages. General capabilities are tracked on MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, and MT-Bench. AgentLM-70B reaches held-in overall 2.55 (vs Llama-2-70B 2.11, GPT-4 2.13) and held-out overall 1.40 (+176% over Llama-2-70B's 0.51), comparable to GPT-3.5's 1.49, while general overall stays 0.96 (+1% vs Llama-2). Held-out gains scale with size: 7B +76%, 13B +57%, 70B +176%. On general tasks AgentLM-70B holds MMLU 59.5, GSM8K 59.7, HumanEval 28.7, MT-Bench 7.26. Error analysis shows AgentLM sharply cuts invalid-action and repetition failures.
key_results: AgentLM-70B achieves held-out overall 1.40 (+176% over Llama-2-70B), roughly matching GPT-3.5 (1.49), and held-in overall 2.55, approaching GPT-4 (2.13). General ability is preserved: overall general score 0.96 vs Llama-2's 0.95 (+1%), e.g. MMLU 59.5 and GSM8K 59.7.
evolution_note: AgentTuning (Oct 2023) builds on ReAct (CoT+action prompting), Self-Instruct, FLAN-style instruction tuning, and GPT-4 distillation, and directly reacts to the AgentBench finding that open LLMs trailed GPT-3.5/GPT-4 on agent tasks. As one of the earliest multi-task agent-trajectory SFT works, it anticipates the later wave of agentic post-training and tool-use RL that scales trajectory data and moves from SFT toward reinforcement over environment rewards.
